title: He's Got the Whole World in His Hands
source: African-American spiritual. Text as first printed in Edward Boatner (ed.), Spirituals Triumphant, Old and New (Nashville: Sunday School Publishing Board, National Baptist Convention, 1927), No. 68: the six stanzas whole world, all the power, my mother, my father, the fishes of the sea, the whole church, with the singular "hand". The later stanzas (wind and rain, little bitty baby, you and me) first appear after 1930 and are left out. Stanza list checked against C. Michael Hawn, History of Hymns (UMC Discipleship, 2023), which quotes Boatner's 1927 text. Only the traditional words are used; Boatner's arrangement is not.
